liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Saint of Circumstance** (3 reviews): Reviewer says this is the first live Saint, with verses differing from the studio version; This is the first Saint of Circumstance, with its early lyrics making it interesting [5][15][16]
- **Loser** (2 reviews): Reviewer rates the Loser performance among the best of the show, at five stars; In the first verse Jerry sings ace of diamonds instead of the usual queen [8][15]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): The jam from Drums into Not Fade Away, and the song itself, is called a real highlight; A killer jam after Drums leads into a spectacular Not Fade Away [8][12]
- **El Paso** (1 review): Reviewer, who attended, calls El Paso very nice and says Bobby sang in great voice [11]
- **Easy To Love You** (1 review): This is the first Easy To Love You [16]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Lost Sailor and Saint of Circumstance are joined together for the first time here, according to the reviewer [5]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the weakest first live outing of the Shakedown material they have heard [10]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Reviewer found this performance weak and felt the band played the show without much effort [6]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-08-31.135775.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 178 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1979-08-31.sbd.miller.92924.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 171 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Good soundboard with acceptable patches; needs only standard EQ [12]
- **gd79-08-31.nak.glyde.9973.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 169 min; rated 2.5/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this audience tape poor, with high end that fluctuates as if the tape was damaged; Despite not being taped from prime close spots, every instrument and vocal comes through clearly [7][9]
- **gd1979-08-31.partial.aud.stankiewicz.129030.flac1644**: audience recording; 12 songs; 78 min [4]

## Around the show

- This was the reviewer's first Dead show, and it hooked them for life [7]
- Part of Brent's first run of shows with the band, at the end of summer 1979 [9]
- Reviewer's mother attended and described a crowd of drunk, high school-aged kids; also called the venue strange [10]
- Brent plays Cassidy and Dire Wolf with the band for the first time; reviewer links it to the 1980 acoustic shows [16]
- Saints in later years were played with much more power than this early one [5]
- Recommends the 8 May 1980 Glens Falls show as far better than this one [6]
- Says the Lost Sailor/Saint at the same venue the next year was much better [6]
- Considers it much better than most shows from the mid-to-late 1980s and mid 1990s [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-08-31.135775.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 source matrix by dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:92924), Recording Info: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k),Transfer Info:Dat (Sony R500) -> VXPocket v2… [1]
- **gd1979-08-31.sbd.miller.92924.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [2]. Also: Source chain: Nakamichi 300 to cassette master, then DAT, then CD (shnid 9973); Fills for the start of Promised Land, the end of Estimated Prophet and the start of Eyes come from that source; Rob Eaton lent the DATs [2]
- **gd79-08-31.nak.glyde.9973.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience [3]
- **gd1979-08-31.partial.aud.stankiewicz.129030.flac1644**: taped by Richie Stankiewicz; transferred by Richie Stankiewicz, Andrew F; source: AUD: Set One, AKG D222E's > Nakamichi 550; Set Two, Nak 300's > Nakamichi 550. [4]
